Class SecurityPrincipal

java.lang.Object
org.springframework.security.core.userdetails.User
org.springframework.security.extension.userdetails.SecurityPrincipal
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Cloneable, org.springframework.security.core.CredentialsContainer, org.springframework.security.core.userdetails.UserDetails
public class SecurityPrincipal extends org.springframework.security.core.userdetails.User implements Cloneable
Extended Spring Security User that carries the domain-specific identity (uid, uuid, ukey, ucode) and role/permission information required by the easy-4-java security stack.

Beyond the standard Spring Security username/password/authority trio, this principal exposes:

  • multiple stable user identifiers (uid, uuid, ukey, ucode);
  • role identifier triple (rid, rkey, rcode);
  • lifecycle flags such as bound, initial and verify;
  • a profile map, a permission set, an optional request sign and the latest geographic coordinates captured from the client.

The class is cloneable and is intended to be stored as the authentication principal by Spring Security so that downstream code can rely on a richer type than the default User.

Since:
3.0.0

[@Loong Wan](https://github.com/loong10k)

  • Constructor Details

    • SecurityPrincipal

      public SecurityPrincipal(String username, String password, String... roles)
      Create a principal using a username, password and a variable-arity list of role names. Each role name is converted to a Spring Security SimpleGrantedAuthority.
      Parameters:
      username - the username presented to Spring Security
      password - the (already-encoded) password
      roles - zero or more role names; null triggers an InsufficientAuthenticationException
      See Also:
      • roleAuthorities(List)

    • SecurityPrincipal

      public SecurityPrincipal(String username, String password, Collection<? extends org.springframework.security.core.GrantedAuthority> authorities)
      Create a principal using a pre-built collection of authorities.
      Parameters:
      username - the username presented to Spring Security
      password - the (already-encoded) password
      authorities - the authorities granted to the user

    • SecurityPrincipal

      public SecurityPrincipal(String username, String password, boolean enabled, boolean accountNonExpired, boolean credentialsNonExpired, boolean accountNonLocked, Collection<? extends org.springframework.security.core.GrantedAuthority> authorities)
      Create a principal with full control over the account-status flags.
      Parameters:
      username - the username presented to Spring Security
      password - the (already-encoded) password
      enabled - whether the account is enabled
      accountNonExpired - whether the account is non-expired
      credentialsNonExpired - whether the credentials are non-expired
      accountNonLocked - whether the account is non-locked
      authorities - the authorities granted to the user

    • isAdmin

      public boolean isAdmin()
      Determine whether the user holds the built-in administrator role.

      The check is performed in three places:

      1. the key of any role in getRoles();
      2. the primary role key;
      3. the primary role id.
      Returns:
      true if the user is an administrator

    • toPayload

      public UserProfilePayload toPayload()
      Convert this principal into a serialisable UserProfilePayload.

      The perms collection is defensively copied into a new HashSet; when the profile map is empty a fresh empty map is exposed on the payload, otherwise the same reference is shared.

      Returns:
      a fresh UserProfilePayload that mirrors this principal's user/role/permission state
